lessons.notes_html:
Short and Detailed Questions

The word science is derived from the Latin word Scientia, which means to study and analyse facts in their original form. Science is based on observation and hypothesis, and to establish a scientific law in the light of experiments is called the scientific method.

The important branches of science are physics, chemistry, biology, astronomy, mathematics, agriculture, medicine and geography. Physics deals with matter and energy; chemistry deals with the nature and composition of things; biology is the study of living things; astronomy studies the universe; and medicine deals with human anatomy, diagnosis and cure of diseases.

Jabir Bin Hayyan is said to be the founder of chemistry. He discovered methods to extract metals from ores, prepared nitric acid, sulphuric acid and hydrochloric acid, and was the first chemist who had his own laboratory. Ibn-ul-Haitham discovered the pinhole camera and wrote Kitab-ul-Manazir, a complete book on light, refraction, reflection, lenses and mirrors.

Dr. Abdus Salam was the only Pakistani scientist who won the Nobel Prize. In 1979 he won the Nobel Prize for his work in theoretical physics on the unification of the weak nuclear force and the electromagnetic force. Dr. Abdul Qadeer Khan directed the Kahuta Research Laboratories and, along with other Pakistani scientists, successfully tested nuclear devices at Chaghi on 28 May 1998, as a result of which Pakistan became an atomic power.

Despite all achievements, science is still helpless in several matters. Genetic diseases are still incurable and the study of the genome is not complete; diseases like AIDS and hepatitis could not be controlled and cancer is still incurable. The food problem of mankind could not be solved completely, natural resources are exhausting, nuclear waste disposal is a problem, and natural disasters like earthquakes could not be predicted or controlled.

Technology is the practical application of scientific knowledge to make tools, machines and articles of daily use. Examples of ancient technology are the wheel of the clay-man, the forge of the blacksmith, the spindle of the weaver, the rahat and plough of the farmer, and oarage boats.

Biology is the study of living things. The word biology is derived from two Greek words, bios meaning life and logos meaning arguments. In biology we study the growth, working and reproduction of living things, including man, animals and plants. It is a branch of science because it studies living things systematically through observation and experiment, and it has two main branches: botany, the study of plants, and zoology, the study of animals.

The Holy Quran says: Read! In the name of thy Lord and Cherisher, Who created. Created man, out of a clot of congealed blood. Read! And thy Lord is most Bountiful. He Who taught the use of the Pen. Taught man that which he knew not (Surah 96, verses 1-5). And Allah says: And of every thing We have created pairs: that ye may receive instruction (Surah 51, verse 49). These verses invite man to think, observe and seek knowledge, which is the basis of science.

Physics is that branch of science which deals specially with matter and energy. It is also called the science of measurement because it deals mostly with measurement. Its main branches are mechanics, heat, light, sound and electricity.

Allotropy is the property by which an element is found in more than one physical form in the same state. Carbon is the most common example, which exists in three allotropic forms: diamond, graphite and bucky balls.

The three elements abundantly found in the human body are carbon, hydrogen and oxygen. They combine to form organic compounds such as proteins, carbohydrates and lipids, which work as building material for the bodies of living organisms.

Water expands on freezing because its molecules are less tightly packed in ice than in liquid water. The density of ice at 0 C is 0.918 g/cm3 while that of water is about 1.00 g/cm3, so there is a considerable increase in volume when liquid water changes to solid ice. That is why ice floats on water and pipes can burst in winter.

Water is a universal solvent because it dissolves a variety of substances, so it is extensively used as a solvent in industrial chemical processes and many chemical reactions are carried out in it. Its properties are: it is a clear, colourless and odourless liquid; it has a low freezing point of 0 C and a high boiling point of 100 C; ice floats on water because its density is less than that of water; and its density is maximum at 4 C.

Oxygen is the second most abundant gas in air and is essential for supporting life and the phenomena of burning and rusting. For burning, three things are required: fuel, heat and oxygen. Nitrogen is the major constituent of air; it is relatively inert and acts as an important diluent of air to slow down combustion and corrosion, and it occurs in plants and animals in the form of proteins.

Fats are stored in the adipose tissue of the human body, under the skin and around the internal organs. This stored fat gives energy when food is short and also protects the organs and keeps the body warm.

A transgenic organism is an organism into which a gene from another organism has been transferred by genetic engineering. Such an organism shows the new character of the transferred gene, for example a crop plant that resists insects or disease.

A catalyst changes the speed of a chemical reaction without undergoing any chemical change in its own structure. In living bodies, enzymes act as catalysts and speed up digestion and other life reactions without being used up.

Detailed Questions

Metabolism is the sum of all chemical reactions in a living body. It has two types: anabolism, in which simple substances join to build complex substances and energy is used, and catabolism, in which complex substances break down into simple ones and energy is released.

Digestion is the breaking down of large, insoluble food molecules into small, soluble molecules that the body can absorb. Assimilation is the use of these absorbed food molecules by the body cells for growth, repair and energy.

An enzyme is a biological catalyst, made of protein, which speeds up a chemical reaction in the body without being changed itself. In daily life enzymes digest our food, help in making bread, cheese and curd, and are used in washing powders to remove stains.

Blood has two main components: plasma, the liquid part, and blood cells. The cells are red blood cells which carry oxygen, white blood cells which fight germs, and platelets which clot the blood. Plasma carries food, hormones and waste materials.

DNA is the hereditary material because it carries the genetic information of an organism in the form of genes. When a cell divides, DNA copies itself and passes the same information to the new cells, so children inherit the characters of their parents through DNA.

Genetic engineering is a technique to transfer genes from one organism to another. In agriculture it produces crops that give more yield and resist insects, diseases and harsh weather, and in livestock it produces animals that give more milk and meat and resist disease.

An antibiotic is a chemical compound obtained from microorganisms and used to control infectious diseases caused by bacteria. Its types include penicillins, made by the Penicillium fungus, and cephalosporins, obtained from the fungus Cephalosporium.

Recycling is producing new products from useless wastes or rubbish. Waste paper, glass, plastic and metal are collected, cleaned and remade into useful articles, which saves raw material and energy and keeps the environment clean. Scarce materials are thus used again instead of being thrown away.

Short Questions

The basic components of food are carbohydrates, lipids (fats and oils), proteins, vitamins, mineral salts and water. Carbohydrates and fats supply energy, proteins build and repair the body, and vitamins and minerals keep the body healthy and protect it from disease.

Vitamin B is a group of water soluble vitamins needed for healthy nerves, skin and blood and for releasing energy from food. Its deficiency causes diseases like beri-beri and anaemia, and it must be taken regularly in food because the body cannot store it.

Iron is needed to make haemoglobin in the red blood cells, which carries oxygen from the lungs to all parts of the body. Without enough iron the blood cannot carry sufficient oxygen, which causes anaemia, weakness and tiredness.

Rabies is caused by the bite of a rabid dog (and other rabid animals). The rabies virus attacks the nervous system, so the bite wound must be washed at once and anti-rabies vaccination started without delay.

Insulin is a hormone made in the pancreas which controls the amount of glucose in the blood. It helps the body cells take in glucose and store the extra glucose, and its deficiency causes diabetes, in which blood sugar rises to a harmful level.

Food has six important components. Carbohydrates are the primary source of energy for animals, while fats and oils give more energy and keep the body warm. Proteins, made of amino acids, build and repair tissues. Vitamins and mineral salts are needed in small amounts for health and protection from disease, and water carries food and waste through the body.

Proteins are large compounds made of amino acids and are the building material of the body. They build muscles, skin, blood and enzymes, repair worn-out tissues and help growth. Meat, fish, eggs, milk, pulses and beans are rich sources of protein.

Vitamins are organic compounds needed in very small amounts to keep the body healthy and to protect it from deficiency diseases. Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat soluble, while B and C are water soluble. Vitamin A keeps eyesight healthy, D strengthens bones, C prevents scurvy, and B keeps nerves and blood healthy.

A balanced diet is food that contains all the nutrients - carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals and water - in the right proportions for health and growth. Growing children need more protein and calcium, hard-working labourers need more carbohydrates for energy, and old people need light, easily digested food with enough vitamins and minerals.

Exercise is necessary to maintain human health because it strengthens muscles, heart and lungs and keeps the body active and fit. It improves blood circulation and digestion, controls body weight and removes tiredness, and it also freshens the mind and helps sound sleep.

Endocrine glands bring about coordination in the body through hormones carried by the blood. The thyroid gland controls growth and metabolism through thyroxin, the pancreas controls blood sugar through insulin and glucagon, and the adrenal glands prepare the body for emergency action through epinephrine. AIDS spreads through infected blood, by using infected needles and syringes, from an infected mother to her child, and through unprotected contact with an infected person. It does not spread by eating, shaking hands or living together. Prevention requires tested blood for transfusion, sterilized syringes, and public awareness about its causes and safety measures.

Malaria is prevented by avoiding mosquito bites and by destroying mosquitoes. Use mosquito nets and repellents, cover water containers, drain standing water, spray insecticides in houses and streets, and take complete anti-malarial treatment at once if fever appears.

Cigarette smoke contains many dangerous gases, including nicotine, tar and carbon monoxide, which cause diseases of the lungs and heart. Smoking makes a person addicted through nicotine, damages the lungs, raises the risk of cancer and heart disease, and harms the health of people nearby who breathe the smoke.

Mental diseases affect thinking, feeling and behaviour, and they must be treated like other diseases. They include severe anxiety and depression, in which a person feels constant fear or sadness, and more serious disorders in which a person loses touch with reality. Proper treatment, care and sympathy help such patients recover.

Dengue fever is a viral disease spread by the bite of the Aedes mosquito, which breeds in clean standing water. Its symptoms are sudden high fever, severe headache, pain in the joints and muscles, and skin rash. There is no specific medicine for it, so the patient needs rest, fluids and medical care.

Dengue fever is treated by rest, plenty of fluids and medicines for fever and pain given on a doctor's advice, with hospital care in serious cases. It is prevented by destroying Aedes mosquitoes: cover water containers, remove standing water, use nets and repellents, and keep the surroundings clean.

Dengue Haemorrhagic Fever is the severe form of dengue in which blood vessels leak and bleeding occurs from the nose, gums and skin, with a dangerous fall in platelets. The patient feels severe pain in the abdomen, vomits repeatedly and becomes weak, so urgent hospital treatment with fluids and blood care is needed to save life.

Detailed Questions

The atmosphere is an envelope of gases that covers the earth from all sides and is about 200 km thick. It is made up of about 78 percent nitrogen and 21 percent oxygen, and the remaining one percent consists of water vapour and trace gases like carbon dioxide, hydrogen, argon, helium and ozone. Its four layers are the troposphere, where most weather occurs; the stratosphere, whose upper part contains the ozone layer; the mesosphere, the coldest layer; and the thermosphere, the outermost and hottest layer, where temperature may be as high as 2000 C.

Ozone is a gas present in the upper stratosphere. It forms a protective covering around the earth, which prevents ultraviolet radiations from reaching the earth. Certain chemicals released from refrigerators, air conditioners, spray cans and factories making packing foams are called chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs). CFCs react with ozone, causing its depletion and thinning of the ozone layer. Consequently a greater number of ultraviolet radiations reach the earth, and these radiations may cause cancer and eye diseases.

The greenhouse effect is the phenomenon in which solar radiations of short wavelength enter the atmosphere but heat waves of long wavelength cannot go out, so the temperature inside rises. Its causes are the increase in greenhouse gases like carbon dioxide, chlorofluorocarbons and methane in the air due to industrialization and burning of fossil fuels. Its effects are change in the earth's climate and weather, melting of ice caps and rising sea level, and flooding of coastal areas.

Human activities affect the environment in many ways. Burning of fossil fuels increases carbon dioxide and produces smoke and gases that pollute the air. Industrial wastes, trash and sewage discharged into water bodies cause water pollution, and municipal trash and chemicals cause land pollution. Cutting of forests destroys natural habitats, and rising population increases the demand for food, housing and energy, which puts resources under pressure and lowers the quality of life.

Aquatic pollution is caused when industrial wastes, trash and sewage from cities are discharged into rivers, streams, ponds, lakes and oceans, and when oil spills from tankers and chemical fertilizers and pesticides washed off from crops enter the water. Its effects are the decrease of oxygen in water, death of fish and aquatic plants, and diseases like cholera and typhoid in man. It is controlled by treating domestic, industrial and hospital wastes before throwing them into water, by not throwing waste articles into water bodies, and by enforcing minimum environmental standards on industries.

Fossil fuels are coal, oil and gas, formed from the remains of plants and animals of the remote past buried under the earth. They are used for transport, power generation, agriculture and industry, and natural gas is used in power plants, cement and fertilizer production, and in homes for heating and cooking. Their environmental effects are that burning of fossil fuels produces smoke and gases which pollute the air and increase carbon dioxide, and large areas of fertile land, forests and natural habitats are destroyed during exploration and drilling of coal and oil.

Conservation of resources means the careful use of natural resources so that they last for future generations. Fossil fuels and minerals are non-renewable resources because they cannot be reproduced or take millions of years to reform, and they may end up soon if their excessive use continues. They are conserved by recycling used materials, by substitution with alternatives, by reuse of articles of common use, and by making minimum and only necessary use of resources.

Mechanized farming means cultivation with tractors, tube wells, harvesters and threshers instead of only muscle power, which increases crop yield and production for export and earning money. Dairy, poultry and fish farming provide milk, meat and eggs and are an important part of agriculture in Pakistan. Wildlife conservation means saving wildlife from extinction by re-establishing habitats and marking certain areas as wildlife reserves and national parks, where human interference is strictly prohibited except for education and research. Wildlife is important because it maintains the balance of nature and provides food, medicines and beauty to the environment.

Increase in population causes environmental problems of physical, economic and social nature. Basic necessities of life like clean air, water, housing and food are not properly fulfilled, and facilities of health and education are not available for all. Resources come under pressure and development stops, poverty and poor quality of life increase, forests are destroyed, cities expand, and problems like crime, hunger and sense of deprivation cast very negative effects on society. Migration from rural to urban areas leads to a huge increase in city population and forces many people to live in slums.

lessons.title: Short Answers
lessons.notes_html:
Short Answers

The law of conservation of energy states that energy can neither be created nor destroyed, but it can be changed from one form to another. For example, when a body is taken to a height, gravitational potential energy is stored in it, and when it is dropped, this energy converts into kinetic energy.

The unit of electrical energy is the kilowatt-hour. One kilowatt-hour is the energy consumed when an appliance of one kilowatt power is used for one hour, and it is the unit in which electricity bills are charged.

Environment is the living place of people, including the physical and social factors around them. It includes air, water, land, plants, animals and the social conditions in which people live.

Degradation of environment means the addition of pollution to the environment more than a certain limit, so that the quality of air, water and land falls and the life of plants, animals and man is harmed.

Three conventional methods of producing electricity are hydroelectric power, thermal power and nuclear power. Five non-conventional methods are solar energy, wind energy, tidal energy, geothermal energy and biogas energy.

Three suggestions for the conservation of energy are: avoid unnecessary use of energy, use energy-saving appliances and bulbs, and use public transport and walk for short distances instead of using personal vehicles.

Two suggestions for the safe disposal of nuclear waste are: bury the waste deep underground in sealed containers in safe places away from people and water, and keep it under strict watch so that its radiations cannot reach living things.

Detailed Questions

Energy is the ability of a body to do work. Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion, for example a running cricket ball or flowing water. Potential energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its position, for example a stone lying at a height or water stored in a dam. The moving ball can do work because of its motion, while the stone at a height can do work when it falls.

The different forms of energy are kinetic energy, potential energy, elastic potential energy, chemical energy, heat energy, light energy, electrical energy and nuclear energy. Heat energy is due to the movement of molecules, light energy helps us see things, electrical energy is the energy of moving charges, and nuclear energy is obtained by breaking the nuclei of heavy atoms or by fusion of small nuclei.

Interconversion of energy means the change of energy from one form to another in different conditions. For example, the chemical energy in cells or batteries converts into electrical energy, and the electrical energy in a bulb converts into heat and light. The law of conservation of energy states that energy can neither be created nor destroyed, it only changes its form.

The conventional methods of producing electricity are hydroelectric power, thermal power and nuclear power. In hydroelectric power, water stored in a dam is allowed to fall on turbines, which run generators and produce electricity. This method does not produce pollution, and the water can be used again for irrigation after producing electricity.

Three non-conventional methods of producing electricity are solar energy, in which photocells convert light into electricity; wind energy, in which windmills run generators; and tidal energy, in which the energy of sea tides runs turbines. Other methods are geothermal energy from the heat inside the earth and biogas energy from biomass.

Electrical energy is measured in kilowatt-hours, which is the unit shown on the electricity meter. The meter works on the principle that when current passes through its coils, a magnetic field is produced which rotates an aluminium disc. The speed of the disc depends on the power being used, and the number of revolutions of the disc is counted to show the total energy consumed in kilowatt-hours.

Thermal pollution is the addition of heat and harmful gases to the atmosphere. It is produced when hot water from power stations and factories is thrown into rivers and when fossil fuels are burnt, which raises the temperature of air and water. It affects the environment by disturbing aquatic life, reducing oxygen in water and increasing the temperature of the surroundings.

Nuclear fuel hazards are the dangers of radiations from nuclear fuel and nuclear waste, which can cause cancer and other diseases and harm living things for a long time. Nuclear waste must be disposed of safely in sealed containers deep underground. Conservation of energy means avoiding unnecessary use of energy, using energy-saving devices, and using public transport, so that energy resources last longer and pollution is reduced.

Short Answers

Electric current is the amount of charge passing through any cross-section of a conductor in one second. Its unit is the ampere, and it is measured by an ammeter connected in series with the circuit.

Potential difference is the energy consumed by one coulomb of charge in moving from one point to another. It is also called voltage, and its unit is the volt. It is measured by a voltmeter connected in parallel with the circuit.

Ohm's law relates three quantities: potential difference, current and resistance. It states that the current flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across its ends, provided its temperature remains constant, and resistance is the constant in this relation.

Resistance is the opposition to the flow of charges through a conductor. Its SI unit is the ohm. Conductors of large resistance are called resistors.

Resistors are conductors of large resistance, used in circuits to control the current. They are used in radios, televisions and other electrical appliances to reduce current to the required value.

Charging of a capacitor means storing charge on its plates. When a capacitor is connected to a battery, charge flows to its plates until the potential difference between the plates becomes equal to the battery voltage, and the charge stored is proportional to the potential difference.

Gang capacitors are used in radios for tuning. By changing the capacitance of the gang capacitor, the radio is tuned to the required station, because the tuning circuit then receives only the signals of that frequency.

A step-up transformer increases the alternating voltage. It has more turns in its secondary coil than in its primary coil, so the output voltage is higher than the input voltage.

A step-down transformer decreases the alternating voltage. It has fewer turns in its secondary coil than in its primary coil, so the output voltage is lower than the input voltage.

A shunt resistance is connected in parallel with a galvanometer to convert it into an ammeter. Most of the current passes through the low shunt resistance, while only a small safe current passes through the galvanometer, so the galvanometer can measure large currents.

Detailed Questions

Electric current is the flow of charge through a conductor, measured as the amount of charge passing through any cross-section in one second. Conventional current is the flow of positive charge from higher potential to lower potential. In a metal wire electrons actually flow from lower to higher potential, but by convention the current is taken as flowing from the positive terminal to the negative terminal.

Potential difference between two points is the energy consumed by one coulomb of charge in moving from one point to the other. For example, if one joule of energy is consumed by one coulomb of charge in moving between two points, the potential difference is one volt. Its unit is the volt, and it is measured by a voltmeter.

Resistance is the opposition offered by a conductor to the flow of charges. The unit of resistance is the ohm. One ohm is the resistance of a conductor when a potential difference of one volt across its ends causes a current of one ampere to flow through it.

A capacitor is a device that stores charge. It consists of two plates separated by an insulator, and the charge stored on it is proportional to the potential difference between its plates. Capacitors are used in radios for tuning, in fans and motors for starting, in flash cameras, and in power supply circuits for smoothing.

Direct current is current that flows in one direction only, for example current from a cell or battery. Alternating current is current that changes its direction again and again, for example the current supplied to our homes. Direct current voltage cannot be changed by a transformer, while alternating voltage can be increased or decreased by a transformer.

A voltmeter is connected in parallel with a circuit and has a very high resistance, so it takes almost no current and measures potential difference. An ammeter is connected in series with a circuit and has a very low resistance, so it does not disturb the current and measures the current flowing through the circuit.

A multimeter is an instrument for measuring current, voltage and resistance. It is used to test circuits and appliances and to find faults in them. An analogue meter shows a continuous reading with the help of a pointer on a scale, while a digital meter displays the reading in digits on a screen.

An n-type semi-conductor is a semi-conductor in which current is mostly due to free electrons, obtained by doping silicon with a pentavalent impurity. A p-type semi-conductor is one in which current is mostly due to holes, obtained by doping silicon with a trivalent impurity. They are used to make diodes, transistors and other electronic devices like radios, televisions and computers.

A diode is forward biased when its p-side is connected to the positive terminal and n-side to the negative terminal of a battery, so current flows easily. It is reverse biased when the connections are reversed, so almost no current flows. Different kinds of diodes are the P-N junction diode used as a rectifier to convert A.C. into D.C., the light emitting diode used in displays and indicators, and the photo diode used in light-measuring devices.

Radio waves are a type of electromagnetic waves, also called carrier waves. Radio transmissions reach us when sound is converted into electrical signals, which are carried by radio waves from a transmitter through the air to a receiver. The receiver separates the sound signals from the carrier waves and changes them back into sound through a speaker.

Television works by converting pictures and sound into electrical signals at the transmitting station, sending them through space or cable, and changing them back into pictures and sound at the receiver. In satellite T.V., signals are transmitted to a geostationary satellite through microwaves by a ground station. The satellite retransmits them to the required ground station after amplifying them, from where they are transmitted onwards to homes.

Television is an electronic system for sending pictures and sound from one place to another. The camera changes pictures into electrical signals and the microphone changes sound into electrical signals. These signals are transmitted by radio waves or cable to receivers, where the picture tube changes the video signals back into pictures on the screen and the speaker changes the audio signals back into sound.

The main parts of a computer are the input devices, the central processing unit, the output devices and the information storage devices. Input devices like the keyboard feed data into the computer; the central processing unit, including the microprocessor, processes the data; output devices like the monitor and printer display or print the results; and storage devices like the hard disk, floppy disk and C.D. store data for later use.

A communication system is an electronic method to transmit information from one place to another. Its main sources are radio, television, telephone, fax machine, computer and Internet. Information is transmitted after converting it into electrical signals, which are sent through wires, radio signals through air, or light signals through optical fibres. Telecommunication is the method used for instant communication of information to far off places.

lessons.title: Detailed Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Detailed Questions

Laser is an abbreviation of light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation. It is an intense beam of light in which all the waves have the same wavelength and all are in phase, and it travels in one direction without spreading. Its important uses are: in surgery as a light scalpel for cutting and coagulation, in ophthalmology for cataract and glaucoma operations, in dermatology for skin diseases, in dentistry, in treating cancer and crushing gallstones and kidney stones, in drilling holes in hard materials like steel and diamond, in making holograms, and in laser-guided missiles and communication.

An optical fibre is a fine fibre of glass used to carry light signals. In construction it has a central core of glass surrounded by a cladding of glass of lower refractive index, covered by a protective coating. Its principle is total internal reflection: when light enters one end of the fibre at a suitable angle, it is reflected again and again inside the core and comes out of the other end without loss. In working, light signals carrying information are sent into the fibre and travel through it by repeated total internal reflection to the other end.

Radar system means radio detection and ranging. It works by sending radio waves towards an object and receiving the waves reflected back from it. From the time taken by the waves to return, the distance, direction and speed of the object are found. Its uses are in airports for guiding aeroplanes, in ships for finding other ships and icebergs, in the army for detecting enemy aeroplanes and missiles, and in weather forecasting.

A satellite is an object placed in orbit around the earth to receive signals from a ground station and retransmit them after amplifying. Its types are communication satellites, which facilitate television, telephone and radio communication; weather satellites, which help in weather prediction; and scientific satellites, which study the universe, galaxies, stars and planets. Their uses are in communication, weather forecasting, exploration of natural resources, television transmission and scientific research.

Radioactivity is the emission of radiations from the nucleus of an atom. There are three types of radiations. Alpha radiations are positively charged particles, deflected towards the negative plate, and they have low penetrating power. Beta radiations are negatively charged particles, deflected towards the positive plate, and they have greater penetrating power than alpha rays. Gamma radiations have no charge, are not affected by any field, and have the greatest penetrating power.

Radioisotopes are the radioactive isotopes of elements, whose nuclei emit radiations. Their uses are in medicine for diagnosis and treatment of diseases like cancer, in agriculture for producing better varieties of crops and preserving food, in industry for checking the thickness of materials and finding faults, and in research for tracing chemical reactions.

X-rays are obtained when fast-moving electrons strike a metal target in an X-ray tube, which produces high-energy radiations. Their properties are that they can pass through flesh but are stopped by bones and dense materials, they affect photographic film, and they travel in straight lines. Their uses are in medicine for seeing broken bones and internal organs, in industry for finding faults inside materials, and in security checking of luggage.

X-rays give a flat, two-dimensional picture of the inside of the body on a film, while a C.T. scan uses X-rays from many angles and a computer to make detailed cross-sectional pictures of the body. The C.T. scan is better for treatment because it shows the exact position, size and shape of a disease or injury inside the body, which an ordinary X-ray cannot show clearly.

The steel mill is important because steel is needed for construction, machines, vehicles, ships, tools and many other articles of daily use. Pakistan Steel Mills produces iron and steel from iron ore, which makes the country self-sufficient in steel, provides employment to thousands of workers, and supports other industries like engineering, construction and transport.

The pharmaceutical industry makes medicines for the treatment of diseases. In Pakistan it produces tablets, capsules, syrups and injections, and it also makes radio pharmaceuticals for medical use. This industry is important because it provides life-saving drugs at home, reduces dependence on imported medicines, and provides employment to chemists, pharmacists and other workers.

Synthetic fibres are man-made fibres produced by chemical processes from petroleum products, unlike natural fibres obtained from plants and animals. Examples are nylon, polyester and rayon. They are strong, durable and easy to wash, and they are used for making clothes, ropes, carpets and many other articles.

The important sections of the textile industry are spinning, in which yarn is made from cotton; weaving, in which cloth is made from yarn; dyeing and printing, in which cloth is coloured and designed; and stitching, in which garments are made. Pakistan's textile industry is very important because it earns a large amount of foreign exchange and provides employment to millions of workers.

The leather industry makes leather from the skins of animals by tanning, and then makes shoes, bags, jackets, gloves and other articles from it. Pakistan's leather industry is important because it earns foreign exchange through exports and provides employment. Its centres are in Lahore, Karachi and Sialkot, where sports goods and leather garments are also made.

Sugar processing starts with sugarcane, which is crushed in mills to obtain juice. The juice is cleaned, heated and concentrated by evaporation, and then sugar crystals are formed by cooling. The crystals are separated by centrifuge machines, dried and packed as sugar. The leftover molasses is used for making alcohol and other products, and the bagasse is used as fuel in the mills.

lessons.notes_html:
Brief Answers

The Viking space probes collected soil and rock samples from the surface of Mars and tested them for signs of life. Their landers scooped up Martian soil, analysed its chemicals and sent the results and pictures back to the earth.

The Hubble telescope is a space telescope launched into space on 24 April 1990 with the help of the space shuttle Discovery. The size of its mirror is 2.5 metres and its weight is 11 tonnes. It observes stars, galaxies and planets from above the earth's atmosphere without disturbance.

Some advantages of artificial satellites are: they facilitate television, telephone and radio communication to far off places; they help in weather prediction and warning about cyclones; they help in exploration of natural resources hidden in the earth; and they help scientists study stars, planets, galaxies and cosmic rays.

The basic objectives of SUPARCO include space research, study of the ozone layer, study of pollution of the atmosphere, astronomy, study of radio waves, exploration of natural mineral resources through geographic information technology, establishment of ground stations, and launching of space rockets and satellites into space for various purposes.

Pakistan's nuclear power plants are located at Karachi and Chashma. The first nuclear power plant was established at Karachi in 1972 with a total production capacity of 137 megawatts, and later plants were set up at Chashma to increase the production of nuclear electricity.

Detailed Questions

The space programme is important because information collected by space research is very beneficial for the scientific development of any country. Artificial satellites are useful for television, telephone and radio communication, weather forecasting, exploration of mineral resources, study of the ozone layer and pollution, and scientific study of the universe. Space stations help in studying the natural resources hidden in the earth and the planets of the solar system.

Pakistan's space programme is looked after by SUPARCO, the Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission, established in 1961 in collaboration with the Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission, with its headquarters at Karachi. Pakistan launched its first rocket, Rahber, into space on 7 June 1962, and by now more than 200 rockets have been launched, hovering from 20 to 550 kilometres. In 1973 three Skua rockets were sent into space to measure air pressure and temperature. In July 1990 Pakistan launched its indigenous artificial satellite Badar-1, and SUPARCO established earth stations at Karachi, Lahore and Rawat for getting information from satellites.

The Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission was established in 1956 for the use of nuclear energy for peaceful purposes. Its services are: production of electricity through nuclear power plants at Karachi and Chashma; use of radioisotopes and radiopharmaceuticals in medicine, agriculture and industry; research in nuclear science at PINSTECH, established in 1965; and preparation of special nuclear materials and sophisticated instruments on a limited scale for the needs of the country.
